workflows.description: Boots the project so its preview is ready to inspect.

steps.prompt:
Look at the issue and classify it by setting a label.
Use "bug" if it is clearly a feature that is implemented but has a bug.
Use "enhancement" if this is a new feature.
Use "docs" if there is something off with the Readme.
steps.label: Classify Issue

steps.prompt: Fix the provided Issue and report back with a Link to the PR and Preview
steps.label: Fix Bug

steps.prompt: Make a plan for the provided issue and report back into the issue to get an approval.
steps.label: Add Enhancement

steps.prompt:
Read the ticket of this session. Try to reproduce it in the preview and in the code. Do not fix anything. Then apply exactly one label: "bug" if something is broken, "enhancement" if it was never built and then move it to "To Do".

If the ticket lacks the details to decide, apply no label and ask the reporter in a comment for clarification. Never apply a label and ask a question.
steps.label: Triage

steps.prompt:
The ticket of this session was confirmed as a bug. When you are beginning your work move the Ticket to "In Progress". Then fix it on a work branch, verify the fix on the preview, commit in logical batches, and open a pull request. 

Comment a short summary of the change on the ticket and move it to "In Review".
steps.label: Bug Fix

steps.prompt:
The ticket of this session is an enhancement. 
Work out how it would be built in this project: the files to touch, the steps in order, and what is open. 
Do not change any files or the status. Just post the plan as a comment, written for the person who reported the ticket.
steps.label: Plan Enhancement

items.output:
# Styles

- Project CSS is only `src/css/app.css`: `@import "tailwindcss";` + `@source "../../templates";`.
  Tailwind v4, no `tailwind.config.js`, no `@theme` block -> there are no project color
  utilities (`text-accent` etc. do NOT exist).
- Most visual styling comes from the remote Knecht styleguide loaded in
  `templates/_layouts/default.twig`: `https://knecht.works/styleguide/kit.css` (+ `kit.js`),
  applied through `<body class="kit-body kit-light">`.
- Kit color tokens (light mode values): `--kit-accent` #b7f8a2 (too pale on white),
  `--kit-accent-strong` #527f54 (the readable accent, used by `.kit-text-accent` and by
  `.kit-body a`), `--kit-mint` #6ba96d, `--kit-orange` #fa7a2c, `--kit-amber` #fcc46e.
- `.kit-badge` derives text, border and background from `--kit-mint`; recolor a single badge
  by overriding that variable inline (e.g. `style="--kit-mint: var(--kit-orange)"`) so all
  three stay consistent.
- Nav links used to carry Tailwind's important utility `text-black!`, hardcoding black text
  that broke in dark mode. Fixed (September 2026) with inline `style="color: var(--kit-ink)"`
  instead: the kit.css rule `.kit-body a:not(.kit-button)` has higher specificity than any
  single `.kit-*` class (e.g. `.kit-text-ink`), so a plain class override loses; an inline
  style always wins over a non-`!important` external rule regardless of specificity, and
  `--kit-ink` already flips value with `.kit-light`, so the color now follows the theme.
- Dark mode added (November 2026, CC-45). Kit.css defaults to dark; adding `.kit-light` to
  any wrapper (we use `<html>`, not `<body>`) flips to light tokens. There is no `.kit-dark`
  class to add for dark mode - it's just the absence of `.kit-light`. `kit.js`'s
  `KnechtKit.toggleTheme()` toggles this class on `document.body` specifically; we do our
  own toggle on `document.documentElement` instead (in `src/js/app.js`) so an inline
  `<script>` in `<head>` (both `templates/_layouts/default.twig` and `templates/index.twig`)
  can set the class before `<body>` exists, avoiding a flash of the wrong theme. Preference
  is read from `localStorage.theme` (`'light'`/`'dark'`), falling back to
  `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` when unset. The toggle button is `#theme-toggle`
  in the nav (top right); it holds two inline SVG spans (`[data-theme-icon="sun"]` /
  `[data-theme-icon="moon"]`, from the akar-icons/ant-design sets attached to the ticket, not
  emoji) and `src/js/app.js` toggles `hidden` on whichever one doesn't match the active theme
  - the sun shows while dark mode is active (click to go light), the moon while light is
  active (click to go dark).
- Nav links (November 2026) got a hover color via a `.nav-link` class + `.nav-link:hover`
  rule in `src/css/app.css`, with `!important` because it must beat the links' inline
  `style="color: var(--kit-ink)"`.
- Changing Tailwind utilities/arbitrary values requires a Vite build (`ddev npm run build`)
  unless the dev server is running. Using `kit-*` classes or inline CSS variables needs no
  build at all - prefer them when a rebuild is unwanted.
- `craft.vite.script()` never emits a CSS `<link>` when the dev server is running (its
  `devServerScript()` only returns the JS module tag); Vite injects Tailwind's CSS via JS
  after `app.js` executes, causing a flash of unstyled content on every navigation. Fixed in
  `templates/_layouts/default.twig` by adding `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{
  craft.vite.asset('src/css/app.css') }}">` when `craft.vite.devServerRunning()` is true -
  requesting a Vite dev-server `.css` path via a real stylesheet link (browsers send
  `Sec-Fetch-Dest: style`) makes Vite return actual `text/css` instead of the JS-injection
  shim, so it loads render-blocking like a production build.
# Templates

- Small Craft CMS fixture. Single layout `templates/_layouts/default.twig` holds head, the
  whole navigation (`{% block navigation %}`), hero and content blocks.
- `templates/_entry.twig` routes an entry to `_pages/<section>/<entryType>` ->
  `_pages/<section>/default`; those page templates

items.text:
I added a dark mode toggle to the nav, top right. I haven't loaded the page in a browser or run a build, so it is untested.

- **Toggle:** a `#theme-toggle` button shows a sun icon in dark mode and a moon icon in light mode. Clicking it switches the theme.
- **Saved choice:** the choice is stored in `localStorage.theme`. If nothing is stored, it follows the system `prefers-color-scheme`.
- **No flash:** a small inline script in `<head>` sets the theme class on `<html>` before the page renders.
- **Page default:** I removed the hardcoded `kit-light` from `<body>`. The page now starts dark or light according to the saved choice or system setting, where it was always light before.
- **Nav links:** I replaced `text-black!` with `style="color: var(--kit-ink)"`, because black text was unreadable in dark mode.

The changes are in `templates/_layouts/default.twig` and `src/js/app.js`. They are uncommitted in the working tree, and there is no open PR.

`templates/index.twig` is a standalone page that doesn't use the layout. I didn't change it, so it has no toggle.

The project memory says dark mode was already added in CC-45. The code had no toggle, so that note looks stale. I haven't updated it.
